1. Open Android Studio and select **Open**.

2. Run the Gradle wrapper script in the project root:
```bash
./gradlew assembleDebug
```

3. After a successful build, you will find the generated APK file at:
`app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`

*Note: You can install the debug APK on an emulator or an Android device via USB by running `./gradlew installDebug` or by dragging and dropping the APK file into an emulator.*

11: /**
12:  * Extracts facial embeddings using a LiteRT MobileFaceNet model.
13:  * 
14:  * MobileFaceNet provides a balance of speed and accuracy, generating a
15:  * 192-dimensional vector representation of a face. We use LiteRT (com.google.ai.edge.litert)
16:  * for the inference execution as requested.
17:  */
18: class FaceEmbeddingExtractor(context: Context) {
19:     private val interpreter: Interpreter
20:     
21:     init {
22:         // Load the tflite model from the assets folder.
23:         // Requires android.aaptOptions.noCompress "tflite" in build.gradle.kts to avoid compression.
24:         val assetFileDescriptor = context.assets.openFd("mobile_face_net.tflite")
25:         val fileInputStream = FileInputStream(assetFileDescriptor.fileDescriptor)
26:         val fileChannel = fileInputStream.channel
27:         val startOffset = assetFileDescriptor.startOffset
28:         val declaredLength = assetFileDescriptor.declaredLength
29:         val mappedByteBuffer = fileChannel.map(FileChannel.MapMode.READ_ONLY, startOffset, declaredLength)
30:         
31:         interpreter = Interpreter(mappedByteBuffer)
32:     }
33: 
34:     /**
35:      * Extracts a 192-dim face embedding from a cropped face bitmap.
36:      * The input bitmap should ideally be cropped exactly to the bounding box
37:      * returned by ML Kit, and will be resized to 112x112 internally.
38:      */
39:     fun extractEmbedding(faceBitmap: Bitmap): FloatArray {
40:         // MobileFaceNet input is 112x112 RGB
41:         val resizedBitmap = Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(faceBitmap, 112, 112, true)
42:         
43:         // 1 batch, 112 height, 112 width, 3 channels, 4 bytes per float
44:         val inputBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(1 * 112 * 112 * 3 * 4)
45:         inputBuffer.order(ByteOrder.nativeOrder())
46:         
47:         val intValues = IntArray(112 * 112)
48:         resizedBitmap.getPixels(intValues, 0, 112, 0, 0, 112, 112)
49:         
50:         // MobileFaceNet normalization: (pixel - 127.5) / 128.0
51:         for (pixelValue in intValues) {
52:             val r = ((pixelValue shr 16 and 0xFF) - 127.5f) / 128.0f
53:             val g = ((pixelValue shr 8 and 0xFF) - 127.5f) / 128.0f
54:             val b = ((pixelValue and 0xFF) - 127.5f) / 128.0f
55:             
56:             inputBuffer.putFloat(r)
57:             inputBuffer.putFloat(g)
58:             inputBuffer.putFloat(b)
59:         }
60:         
61:         // Output is typically [1, 192]
62:         val outputBuffer = Array(1) { FloatArray(192) }
63:         
64:         interpreter.run(inputBuffer, outputBuffer)
65:         
66:         return outputBuffer[0]
67:     }
68:     
69:     fun close() {
70:         interpreter.close()
71:     }
72: }

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.*
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.material3.Button
import androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.PasswordVisualTransformation
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.compose.collectAsStateWithLifecycle
import com.salarybox.app.data.model.Role

@Composable
fun LoginScreen(
    viewModel: LoginViewModel,
    onLoginSuccess: (Role) -> Unit
) {
    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()

    Column(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .padding(24.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.Center
    ) {
        Text("SalaryBox", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineLarge)
        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(32.dp))

        OutlinedTextField(
            value = uiState.username,
            onValueChange = viewModel::onUsernameChange,
            label = { Text("Username") },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
        )

        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))

        OutlinedTextField(
            value = uiState.password,
            onValueChange = viewModel::onPasswordChange,
            label = { Text("Password") },
            visualTransformation = PasswordVisualTransformation(),
            keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Password),
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
        )

        if (uiState.error != null) {
            Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(8.dp))
            Text(
                text = uiState.error!!,
                color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error,
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium
            )
        }

        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(32.dp))

        Button(
            onClick = { viewModel.login(onSuccess = onLoginSuccess) },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
            enabled = !uiState.isLoading
        ) {
            if (uiState.isLoading) {
                CircularProgressIndicator(
                    modifier = Modifier.size(24.dp),
                    color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimary
                )
            } else {
                Text("Login")
            }
        }
    }
}

# SalaryBox — Requirements Audit

## Summary
The data layer and business logic are solid. The core issues are in the **staff login flow** — there is no proper per-staff login, so a staff member can't authenticate and see *their own* attendance. All fixes are UI/ViewModel level.

---

## Requirement 1 ✅ — Login Screen
**Status: WORKS** (just fixed). Admin login with `admin / admin123`, Staff login with `staff / staff123` (seeded in `AppDatabase`).

> **Known issue being fixed:** `LoginViewModel.init` was seeding `admin / 123` but the DB already seeds `admin / admin123`. Removing the conflicting seed.

---

## Requirement 2 ✅ — Admin: View staff, Add staff, Open profile
**Status: WORKS.**
- `AdminHomeScreen` → `StaffListScreen` → tap card → `StaffProfileScreen` ✅
- `StaffListScreen` FAB → `AddStaffScreen` ✅

---

## Requirement 3 ✅ — Admin: Enrol staff face
**Status: WORKS** (infrastructure is fully built).
- `StaffProfileScreen` has an "Enrol Face" button → opens `CameraCaptureScreen`
- ML Kit detects face, `FaceEmbeddingExtractor` extracts embedding, saves to DB ✅

---

## Requirement 4 ❌ — Staff: Mark attendance only if face matches
**Status: BROKEN — the staff login flow is wrong.**

### Root Cause
When a staff user logs in, they land on `StaffHomeScreen` which shows a **"Simulate Logged-In User" dropdown** to pick any staff member. This is a demo artifact — it doesn't use the logged-in user's identity at all.

### Fix needed
- Pass the logged-in `staffId` (from the `UserEntity`) through to `StaffHomeScreen` and `MarkAttendanceScreen`
- The `User` table and `Staff` table are separate — need to link them (either by `employeeId` or by adding a `staffId` FK to `UserEntity`)
- Simplest fix: When staff logs in, look up their staff record by matching `username == employeeId` or store `staffId` in `UserEntity`

### Plan
1. Add `staffId: Long?` to `UserEntity` (DB migration version 2)
2. When admin creates a staff member, also create a user account with `role=STAFF`, `username=employeeId`, `password="1234"` (default), and link `staffId`
3. On staff login, navigate directly to their `StaffHomeScreen` pre-loaded with their own `staffId`

---

## Requirement 5 ✅ — Store timestamp, selfie and location on attendance
**Status: WORKS.**
- `AttendanceEntity` has `timestamp`, `selfiePath`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `matchConfidence`
- `MarkAttendanceViewModel.processAttendanceCapture` saves all these ✅
- `AttendanceHistoryScreen` displays them ✅

---

## Changes to implement

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `UserEntity.kt` | Add `staffId: Long? = null` |
| `AppDatabase.kt` | Bump version to 2, add migration, remove conflicting seed |
| `LoginViewModel.kt` | Remove conflicting seed logic |
| `AddStaffScreen.kt` | Auto-create staff user account on save |
| `StaffViewModel.kt` | Expose `addStaff` that also creates a linked user |
| `StaffHomeScreen.kt` | Accept a real `staffId` param, remove the dropdown |
| `MainActivity.kt` | Pass logged-in user's `staffId` from login result |
| `AuthRepository.kt` | Add method to look up user's linked staffId |

12:  * Extracts facial embeddings using a LiteRT MobileFaceNet model.
13:  * 
14:  * MobileFaceNet provides a balance of speed and accuracy, generating a

18: class FaceEmbeddingExtractor(context: Context) {
19:     private val interpreter: Interpreter
20:     
21:     init {
22:         // Load the tflite model from the assets folder.
23:         // Requires android.aaptOptions.noCompress "tflite" in build.gradle.kts to avoid compression.
24:         val assetFileDescriptor = context.assets.openFd("mobile_face_net.tflite")
25:         val fileInputStream = FileInputStream(assetFileDescriptor.fileDescriptor)
26:         val fileChannel = fileInputStream.channel
27:         val startOffset = assetFileDescriptor.startOffset
28:         val declaredLength = assetFileDescriptor.declaredLength
29:         val mappedByteBuffer = fileChannel.map(FileChannel.MapMode.READ_ONLY, startOffset, declaredLength)
30:         
31:         interpreter = Interpreter(mappedByteBuffer)
32:     }
33: 
34:     /**
35:      * Extracts a 192-dim face embedding from a cropped face bitmap.
36:      * The input bitmap should ideally be cropped exactly to the bounding box
37:      * returned by ML Kit, and will be resized to 112x112 internally.
38:      */
39:     fun extractEmbedding(faceBitmap: Bitmap): FloatArray {
40:         // MobileFaceNet input is 112x112 RGB
41:         val resizedBitmap = Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(faceBitmap, 112, 112, true)
42:         
43:         // 1 batch, 112 height, 112 width, 3 channels, 4 bytes per float
44:         val inputBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(1 * 112 * 112 * 3 * 4)
45:         inputBuffer.order(ByteOrder.nativeOrder())
46:         
47:         val intValues = IntArray(112 * 112)
48:         resizedBitmap.getPixels(intValues, 0, 112, 0, 0, 112, 112)
49:         
50:         // MobileFaceNet normalization: (pixel - 127.5) / 128.0
51:         for (pixelValue in intValues) {
52:             val r = ((pixelValue shr 16 and 0xFF) - 127.5f) / 128.0f
53:             val g = ((pixelValue shr 8 and 0xFF) - 127.5f) / 128.0f
54:             val b = ((pixelValue and 0xFF) - 127.5f) / 128.0f
55:             
56:             inputBuffer.putFloat(r)
57:             inputBuffer.putFloat(g)
58:             inputBuffer.putFloat(b)
59:         }
60:         
61:         // Output is typically [1, 192]
62:         val outputBuffer = Array(1) { FloatArray(192) }
63:         
64:         interpreter.run(inputBuffer, outputBuffer)
65:         
66:         return outputBuffer[0]
67:     }

`mobile_face_net.tflite` is a lightweight, pre-trained TensorFlow Lite model commonly used for **face recognition** in mobile applications[1][2][3]. It is designed to run efficiently on resource-constrained devices, such as Android and iOS, by generating facial embeddings (feature vectors) from images[1][4][3].

### Common Uses & Context
*   **Face Recognition:** It typically takes a cropped face image (often 112x112 pixels) as input and outputs a facial vector (e.g., 192 dimensions), which can be used to compare and identify faces by calculating the distance between vectors[1][4][5].
*   **Mobile Development:** It is frequently integrated into Flutter or Android projects alongside face detection libraries (like Google ML Kit) to perform end-to-end identity verification offline[6][7][8].

### Finding `mobile_face_net.tflite` on GitHub
Because `mobile_face_net.tflite` is a generic name for a model file, it appears in many different open-source repositories where developers have shared their implementations[1][9][8]. You can find it by searching GitHub for the filename directly:

*   **[Search GitHub for "mobile_face_net.tflite"](https://github.com/search?q=mobile_face_net.tflite&type=repositories)**

**Notable projects that include this model (or similar implementations) include:**
*   [Real-Time Face Recognition Android](https://github.com/atharvakale31/Face_Recognition_Android)[8]
*   [Flutter Face Detection & Recognition](https://github.com/Mahesh-R-Mesta/Image-recognition-app)[1]

I've found the root cause of the crash and fixed it! 

Here is what was going wrong:
When you tapped on an employee card to open their profile, the app immediately initialized the `FaceEmbeddingExtractor` class, which loads the `mobile_face_net.tflite` model from the `assets/` folder. 

However, it turns out that the `.tflite` file that was downloaded during the initial project setup wasn't actually a valid AI model—it was an **HTML Error Page** (most likely caused by a broken GitHub link fetching a `404 Not Found` page instead of the actual file). Because of this, the TensorFlow Lite Interpreter crashed instantly with a `ByteBuffer is not a valid TensorFlow Lite model flatbuffer` exception, causing the app to force-close.

### How I fixed it:
1. I fetched a proper, valid `mobile_face_net.tflite` model file from a reliable repository and replaced the corrupted file in `app/src/main/assets/`.
2. I successfully rebuilt the APK with the valid model bundled inside.

You can now click the **Run** button in Android Studio to install the updated app. The staff profile screen will load properly and you will be able to enroll a staff member's face via the camera!

package com.salarybox.app.ui.login

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.*
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.material3.Button
import androidx.compose.material3.CircularProgressIndicator
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.PasswordVisualTransformation
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.lifecycle.compose.collectAsStateWithLifecycle
import com.salarybox.app.data.model.Role

@Composable
fun LoginScreen(
    viewModel: LoginViewModel,
    onLoginSuccess: (role: Role, staffId: Long?) -> Unit
) {
    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()

    Column(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxSize()
            .padding(24.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.Center
    ) {
        Text("SalaryBox", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineLarge)
        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(32.dp))

        OutlinedTextField(
            value = uiState.username,
            onValueChange = viewModel::onUsernameChange,
            label = { Text("Username") },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
        )

        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))

        OutlinedTextField(
            value = uiState.password,
            onValueChange = viewModel::onPasswordChange,
            label = { Text("Password") },
            visualTransformation = PasswordVisualTransformation(),
            keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Password),
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
        )

        if (uiState.error != null) {
            Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(8.dp))
            Text(
                text = uiState.error!!,
                color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error,
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium
            )
        }

        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(32.dp))

        Button(
            onClick = { viewModel.login(onSuccess = onLoginSuccess) },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
            enabled = !uiState.isLoading
        ) {
            if (uiState.isLoading) {
                CircularProgressIndicator(
                    modifier = Modifier.size(24.dp),
                    color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimary
                )
            } else {
                Text("Login")
            }
        }
        
        Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))
        Text(
            text = "Admin: admin / admin123\nStaff: EmployeeID / 1234",
            color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall
        )
    }
}
